mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower (t-test p > 0.10) when GDPC1 YoY change < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE < 4% for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 3% indicates expanding manufacturing activity, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher (t-test p > 0.05) when INDPRO exceeds its 12-month MA by more than 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their 12-month averages by more than 1% indicates a dual tightening of monetary policy and accelerating inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower (t-test p > 0.10) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month MA by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal income (proxied by RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month signals a sharp contraction in household demand and construction activity, which reduces economic growth and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both fall > 5% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of instances when both RSAFS and HOUST fall by more than 5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 persons per month for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 for five consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1 QoQ SAAR) below 1% for two consecutive quarters indicates subpar economic growth, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 QoQ SAAR < 1% for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower (t-test p > 0.10) when GDPC1 QoQ SAAR < 1% for two consecutive quarters.
